page: Amazon Web Services f2.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro system architecture, tailored for hardware-accelerated processing and memory-intensive enterprise tasks. The host is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, delivering 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory totals 2048.0 GB, which yields an allocation of 10.67 GB per physical core.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by 8 Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ (VU47P) devices providing 640 GB of aggregate accelerator memory. For scratch space and low-latency storage workloads, the instance bundles 7520 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity. Network connectivity is rated at a 100 Gbps baseline bandwidth, while zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The platform concentrates high-density reconfigurable logic, significant RAM capacity, and direct local storage onto a single system. A practical tradeoff is the prerequisite of specialized FPGA bitstreams and development tooling to utilize the accelerators compared to conventional x86 execution. The configuration aligns with custom hardware acceleration, genomic analysis, electronic design automation, real-time video transcoding, and financial analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services f2.48xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for custom hardware acceleration and memory-intensive computation. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, it contains an AMD x86_64 processor operating at 3.4 GHz with 96 physical cores and 192 dedicated vCPUs. The platform integrates 2048.0 GB of system memory alongside 8 Xilinx Virtex UltraScale+ (VU47P) accelerators equipped with 640 GB of aggregate device memory. Local high-speed storage comprises 7520 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Taking full advantage of the specialized hardware requires custom FPGA bitstreams, presenting engineering overhead compared to standard CPU execution. By concentrating dense acceleration logic, high network bandwidth, and multi-terabyte system memory on a single node, the instance targets FPGA-accelerated computing, genomics processing, media transcoding, electronic design automation, and intensive data analytics.
